tracks.narration: Where does f get its biggest value if we are forced to stay on a curve?
Take f equals x plus y, and constrain to the circle x squared plus y squared equals two. The level lines of f are diagonal — every step northeast pushes f up.
Slide a point along the circle. The gradient of f is fixed — it points northeast everywhere. The gradient of g rotates with the point, always pointing straight out from the origin.
At the constrained maximum the two arrows line up. At the constrained minimum they point opposite ways. So at every constrained extremum, the gradient of f is a scalar multiple of the gradient of g.
Set ∇f equal to lambda times ∇g and solve. The system gives x equals y and lambda equals plus or minus one half, landing exactly on the two candidates.
At every constrained extremum, the gradients align — that is the whole trick.
